prompt: For a sample of cafés, daily foot traffic (hundreds of people) has $\bar{x} = 10$, $s_x = 2$; daily sales (hundreds of dollars) has $\bar{y} = 50$, $s_y = 8$; and $r = 0.75$. Use the least-squares line to predict sales (in hundreds of dollars) for a café with foot traffic $x = 12$.
hint: Build the line first: slope $b = r \frac{s_y}{s_x}$, and the line always passes through $(\bar{x}, \bar{y})$.

hints.text: Build the line first: slope $b = r \frac{s_y}{s_x}$, and the line always passes through $(\bar{x}, \bar{y})$.

hints.title: 🪜 Try a simpler one
hints.text: Warm up: if $b = 1$ and the line passes through $(10, 50)$, then $a = 50 - 1(10) = 40$ and at $x = 12$ you get $52$. Same two steps with $b = 3$ here.

explanation: Intercept: the line passes through $(\bar{x}, \bar{y}) = (10, 50)$, so $a = 50 - 3(10) = 20$ and $\hat{y} = 20 + 3x$.

alternativeExplanations.title: Move from the mean point
steps: Each unit of $x$ adds 3 to the prediction, so 2 units add 6.
Start at $\bar{y} = 50$ and add 6: 56. No intercept needed.

alternativeExplanations.title: The trap: forgetting $r$ in the slope
steps: Using $\frac{s_y}{s_x} = 4$ as the slope gives $\hat{y} = 10 + 4x$ and a prediction of 58.
But the slope must be scaled by $r = 0.75$: $b = 3$, not 4.
With the correct slope the prediction is 56.
